data.description:
GURUDWARA SHRI BADI SANGAT PATSHAHI DASVIN SAHIB is situated in Burhanpur city of Madhya Pradesh.

SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI stopped here while moving towards Nanded. Along with GURU SAHIB was BadhShah Bahadur Shah. GURU SAHIB came here through Agra, Chittorhgarh and Ujjain. In those days a Old Sadhu Jeewan Das was living here on the bank of River Tapti. When SHRI GURU TEGBAHADUR SAHIB JI went to Assam, He was along with GURU SAHIB. When some one told him that a Mahapurakh named SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI has come. Listening to the name he ran barefoot. When GURU SAHIB came to know that his disciple is coming, he also stood up from his seat. Jogi came and fell on the feet of GURU SAHIB. GURU SAHIB took him to the diwan. Sangat of Burhanpur was surprised to see this. They though he (GURU SAHIB) might be a Mahapurakh thats why people are coming for his darshans. GURU SAHIB set jogi free from cycle of life and death. GURU SAHIB stopped here for some long time. From here Badhshah went to Nagpur. And GURU SAHIB moved towards Nanded Sahib. Here an Old saroop of SHRI GURU GRANTH SAHIB JI is also preserved on which there is stamp of SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI. Sangat can have darshan of Beed Sahib on Sangrand Day and on GURUPURAB DAYS.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Tekri Sahib
data.address: Neelkanth Colony, Idgah Hills, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh 462030
data.description:
GURUDWARA SHRI TEKRI SAHIB is situated in Bhopal City of Madhya Pradesh.

The original name of Raja Bhoj’s capital was Bhojpal. There lived a man named Ganpat Lal. One day, this man misbehaved with a woman. The woman cursed him, saying, "May God give you leprosy." Some time later, Ganpat Lal developed leprosy all over his body. Despite seeking treatment from all the hakims, vaidyas, and sufis, his leprosy did not heal. Even his family members threw him out of the house, and he came here and started living in a small hut. One day, while Pir Jalaluddin was passing by, Ganpat Lal fell at his feet. Pir Ji said, "Falling at my feet will do nothing for you; only Baba Nanak can save you. So, focus on Baba Nanak Ji." From that moment, Ganpat Lal began chanting "Dhan Guru Nanak, Dhan Guru Nanak" all the time.

One day, hearing Ganpat Lal’s plea, <b>SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI</b> came here. Ganpat Lal fell at GURU SAHIB's feet and said, "GURU SAHIB, I am being punished for my bad deeds. Please have mercy and relieve my suffering." GURU SAHIB asked Bhai Bala Ji to fetch some water. Bhai Bala Ji searched everywhere for water but couldn’t find any. He returned to GURU SAHIB and reported that there was no water to be found. GURU SAHIB then told Bhai Bala Ji, "The water is right in front of you. Go and fill the vessel." Following GURU SAHIB's command, Bhai Bala Ji quickly returned with water.

GURU SAHIB then instructed Bhai Bala Ji to play the rabab, and he himself took the water and sprinkled it on Ganpat Lal. Ganpat Lal began to loudly chant "Dhan Guru Nanak." GURU SAHIB blessed him, saying, "Go, you will be healed." Witnessing this, Ganpat Lal fainted. When he regained consciousness, he noticed that GURU SAHIB was no longer there. However, on the stone where GURU SAHIB had stood, the marks of his feet were visible. The place where the water had appeared is now the site of Gurudwara Shri Baoli Sahib.

GURUDWARA SHRI BAOLI SAHIB is situated in Bhopal City of Madhya Pradesh.

The original name of Raja Bhoj’s capital was Bhojpal. There lived a man named Ganpat Lal. One day, this man misbehaved with a woman. The woman cursed him, saying, "May God give you leprosy." Some time later, Ganpat Lal developed leprosy all over his body. Despite seeking treatment from all the hakims, vaidyas, and sufis, his leprosy did not heal. Even his family members threw him out of the house, and he came here and started living in a small hut(Now Gurudwara Shri Tekri Sahib). One day, while Pir Jalaluddin was passing by, Ganpat Lal fell at his feet. Pir Ji said, "Falling at my feet will do nothing for you; only Baba Nanak can save you. So, focus on Baba Nanak Ji." From that moment, Ganpat Lal began chanting "Dhan Guru Nanak, Dhan Guru Nanak" all the time.

One day, hearing Ganpat Lal’s plea, SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI came here. Ganpat Lal fell at GURU SAHIB's feet and said, "GURU SAHIB, I am being punished for my bad deeds. Please have mercy and relieve my suffering." GURU SAHIB asked Bhai Bala Ji to fetch some water. Bhai Bala Ji searched everywhere for water but couldn’t find any. He returned to GURU SAHIB and reported that there was no water to be found. GURU SAHIB then told Bhai Bala Ji, "The water is right in front of you. Go and fill the vessel." Following GURU SAHIB's command, Bhai Bala Ji quickly returned with water.

GURU SAHIB then instructed Bhai Bala Ji to play the rabab, and he himself took the water and sprinkled it on Ganpat Lal. Ganpat Lal began to loudly chant "Dhan Guru Nanak." GURU SAHIB blessed him, saying, "Go, you will be healed." Witnessing this, Ganpat Lal fainted. When he regained consciousness, he noticed that GURU SAHIB was no longer there. However, on the stone where GURU SAHIB had stood, the marks of his feet were visible. This place where the water had appeared is now the site of Gurudwara Shri Baoli Sahib.

GURUDWARA SRI CHARAN KAMAL SAHIB is situated in Village Jaisinghpura on outer of Distt City Burhanpur.

From here only GURU SAHIB sent Jathedars for taking care of Takhat Shri Anandpur Sahib, Shri Damdamma Sahib, Shri Patna Sahib and Shri Amritsar Sahib. He also sent Mata Sundar Kaur ji along with Bhai Mani Singh to Delhi. Bhai Gurbaksh Singh ji from the family of Baba Budha Ji Sahib also went back to Punjab.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Nanak Ghat Sahib
data.address: Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456003
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Nanak Ghat Sahib is situated in the city of Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh.

SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI and Bhai Mardana Ji reached Ujjain after traveling from the Girnar Mountains of Junagadh via Ahmedabad. The ancient name of Ujjain was Avantipur. It was located on the banks of the Avanti River, which is now known as the Shipra River. This city was a famous city of the ancient kingdom of Avanti. Raja Vikramaditya, after whom the Vikram Samvat calendar is named, was the king of Ujjain. Before him, Raja Bhartrihari renounced his kingdom and became a yogi, handing over the reign to his younger brother Vikramaditya. Bhartrihari's cave in Ujjain is still famous today. The Mahakal Temple here is considered a prominent pilgrimage site for Hindus.

In 1235 AD, Sultan Altutmish looted the temples of Ujjain. In the fifteenth century, a wall was built around the city for protection. When SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI arrived here, the wall was still intact, and the old city was settled around the Mahakal Temple. Nowadays, the old city and the wall have both collapsed, and the city has been resettled in a new location. Bhartrihari's cave was located outside the city, and near the cave was a mosque with a tamarind tree in front of it. Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji set up camp near this tree.

When Raja Bhartrihari learned of Guru Sahib's arrival, he came to meet Guru Sahib and asked him, "How many of the yogis who come here will attain liberation?" Hearing the hymn from Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, peace settled in Bhartrihari's mind, and all his doubts were dispelled.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Kadamsar Sahib
data.address: Ganwadi Rd, near Rural Police Station, Malkapur, Maharashtra 443101
data.description:
GURDWARA SRI SANGAT WARI SAHIB, Malkapur

During the reign of Nimvant in Malkapur, the people were greatly troubled by the salty water in the region. They appealed to the king for a solution. In that kingdom lived a fakir named Lal Shah, in whom the king had great faith. The king summoned the fakir to his court and asked for a solution to the water problem. The fakir told the king that SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, the tenth incarnation of SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, was present in Burhanpur. He also explained to the king that this person was none other than Allah himself. Therefore, the king should go and personally make a request.

Hearing the fakir's advice, the king of Malkapur went to Burhanpur to meet Guru Sahib. He requested Guru Sahib to purify and sweeten the water for the benefit of the entire populace. Guru Sahib accepted the request and decided to visit Malkapur. The king sent his minister to invite Guru Sahib to his palace, but Guru Sahib chose to stay at the current location and summoned the king there. Guru Sahib gave darshan (divine vision) to the congregation at this spot and had a well dug, from which sweet water emerged. As a result, the water throughout Malkapur also became sweet. The tree under which Guru Sahib sat and the well still exist at that location today.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Omkareshwar Sahib
data.address: Mandhata, Madhya Pradesh 451115

Gurdwara Sri Omkareshwar Sahib, is situated in Omkareshwar city Distt Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Marhattaal Sahib
data.address: SH 22, Marhatal, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh 482002
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Marhattaal Sahib, Jabalpur

SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, spreading the message of unity, traveled from Katak to Amar Kantak and then arrived at this place. The journey took them through a dense and terrifying jungle. During this time, Bhai Mardana Ji began to feel homesick and asked GURU SAHIB for permission to return home. Although GURU SAHIB tried to convince him otherwise, Bhai Mardana Ji stubbornly decided to leave.

As Bhai Mardana Ji traveled about eleven kos (approximately 33 kilometers) away from GURU SAHIB, he found himself surrounded by a vast, desolate jungle. This jungle was home to the man-eating Bhil tribe, and within it lived a demon named Kauda. Bhai Mardana Ji was captured by Kauda and taken to his lair. Terrified by Kauda’s fearsome appearance, Bhai Mardana Ji prayed fervently to GURU SAHIB for help. Hearing his plea, GURU SAHIB instantly appeared at the location. With a compassionate gaze from GURU SAHIB, Kauda’s raging fire of evil was extinguished. Seeing GURU SAHIB, Kauda was overwhelmed with remorse for his sins and fell at GURU SAHIB’s feet.

Touched by GURU SAHIB’s feet, Kauda was transformed into a devout being. He sought forgiveness for all his wrongdoings from GURU SAHIB. GURU SAHIB imparted the knowledge of the divine Bani to Kauda, connecting him with the Almighty. Accompanied by Kauda, GURU SAHIB and Bhai Mardana Ji arrived at this sacred place. GURU SAHIB transformed Kauda into a true devotee and established this holy site. After staying here for a few days, GURU SAHIB proceeded to the land of Rohilkhand.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Guptsar Bandi Chhod Sahib
data.address: Manmad, ਮੰਮਦ, Maharashtra 423104
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Guptsar Bandi Chhod Sahib, Manmad

In 1708, Raja Rustam Rao and Bala Rao from Janwara (Bidar, Karnataka) were imprisoned for life in the fort of Satara, under the rule of Raja Shahu. A Sikh guard at the fort would recite the Sukhmani Sahib every day during Amrit Vela (early morning prayers). The two kings listened attentively, especially to the verse, "Satguru Sikh ke bandhan kaatai || Gur ka Sikh bikar te haate ||" (The True Guru cuts the bonds of his Sikh; the Guru saves his Sikh from sins). One day, they asked the guard, "Does your Guru only free the Sikhs from bondage, or does He help others too?" The Sikh guard advised them to bathe early in the morning, chant Satnam Waheguru with pure hearts, and assured them that Guru Sahib would bless them.

The two brothers sincerely prayed to Guru Sahib with devotion. Seeing their dedication, SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI manifested before them and, through divine power, brought them to the land of Manmad, where they descended under a Peepal tree. Guru Sahib threw their shackles into a nearby well and instructed them to meditate on Naam, serve others, and help the needy. He told them to visit Hazur Sahib and meet Jathedar Bhai Santokh Singh Ji, who would assist them. Jathedar Bhai Santokh Singh Ji sent Mata Bhag Kaur Ji with them to Janwara to provide further help.

Later, SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI appeared in a vision to Sant Baba Nidhan Singh Ji, revealing the history and significance of this sacred place, and instructed him to establish and serve this site. In 1930, Baba Ji confirmed the historical markers with the local people, purchased the land, and began the service, eventually founding this sacred Gurdwara.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Bhuda Sahib
data.address: Bilaspur City, Distt :- Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh, India
data.description:
GURUDWARA SHRI BHUDA SAHIB is situated in the old Bilaspur City, Himachal Pradesh.

SHRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR JI along with family (MATA JI & SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI in Childhood) went to Bilaspur to attend the mourning for Raja Dip Chand of Bilaspur. The Dowager Rani Champa of Bilaspur offered to give the GURU SAHIB a piece of land in her state. GURU SAHIB bought the site on payment of Rs 500 (Five Hundred Rupees). The land consisted of the villages of Lodhipur, Mianpur and Sahota. Here on the mound of Makhowal, SHRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR JI raised a new habitation. The new village was named after the GURU SAHIB 's mother, MATA NANAKI JI. Chakk Nanaki later became famous as Anandpur Sahib. In 1954 while creating reservoir for Bhakra Dam the The historic town was submerged in Sutlej River Govind Sagar, and a new town was built upslope of the old. So the Actual GURDWARA SAHIB is not Accessible but Administration had given land to GURDWARA SAHIB here in Now Bilaspur City.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Singh Shaheedan Sahib
data.address: Village Sohana, Airport Road, Mohali, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Singh Shaheedan Sahib is situated in Mohali City Punjab.

Dhan Dhan Amar Shaheed Jathedar Baba Hanuman Singh Ji was born to Mata Harnam Kaur Ji and father Garja Singh Ji Bath on 18 Maghar 1755, in Narang Singh Wala, District Firozpur. After the martyrdom of Akali Phoola Singh Ji in 1823, Baba Hanuman Singh was appointed as the Jathedar of Shri Akal Takht Sahib. Following the death of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, when the Dogras Gulab Singh, Mishr Singh, Lal Singh, and Tej Singh sided with the British, Maharani Jind Kaur wrote a letter to Sardar Sham Singh Attari, the great general of the Sikh Panth. In response, Baba Ji mobilized 32,000 Sikhs for the battlefield.

At Mudki and Ferozshah, fierce battles ensued between the Sikhs and the British. The Sikhs killed more than 10,000 British soldiers in these encounters, marking the first battle of the Sikh Empire against the British rule. The Nihang Singhs of the Budha Dal advanced toward Patiala, where Raja Karam Singh of Patiala had abandoned his Sikh principles and allied with the British. He launched an attack on the Singhs with cannons, causing around 15,000 Sikhs to be martyred. Despite this, the forces pushed forward towards Ghudam.

During the battle of Ghudam against the British, Baba Ji was hit by a cannonball, leaving him gravely wounded. Still, he continued to face the enemy and eventually reached Sohana village via Rajpura. It was there, with thousands of Singhs, that Baba Hanuman Singh Ji attained martyrdom. At the time of his martyrdom, Baba Ji was 90 years old.

data.name: Gurudwara Bhai Daya Singh ate Bhai Dharam Singh Ji
data.address: Dhawani Mohhala, Shahganj Rd, Near Gandhi Putla, Mahavir Chowk, Shahgunj, Gandhi, Aurangabad, Maharashtra 431001
data.description:
Gurudwara Bhai Daya Singh Ate Bhai Dharam Singh Ji, Aurangabad

In 1706, when SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI sent Bhai Daya Singh and Bhai Dharam Singh to deliver the Zafarnama to Aurangzeb, they first reached Aurangabad and set up camp at this place. However, they learned that the emperor had moved to Ahmednagar, so they went there. Upon reaching Ahmednagar, they still couldn't meet the emperor, as no one allowed them to approach Aurangzeb. As a result, they returned to Aurangabad.

At that time, in order to complete the task assigned by Guru Sahib, Bhai Daya Singh Ji and Bhai Dharam Singh Ji decided that Bhai Dharam Singh would return to Punjab to inform Guru Sahib of the situation and seek his advice. Meanwhile, Bhai Daya Singh stayed back in Aurangabad. During this time, while residing in Aurangabad, Bhai Daya Singh successfully managed to deliver the Zafarnama to Aurangzeb through contact with some influential Mughal officials.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Singh Sabha Sahib
data.address: Mangalwara Ghat Road Raja Mohalla, Madhya Pradesh 461001
data.description:
GURUDWARA SHRI SINGH SABHA SAHIB, Hoshangabad. Hoshangabad is also known as Naramdapuram.

During his second Udasi (journey), SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, while uplifting souls, passed through Betma, Indore, and Bhopal, eventually arriving at Hoshangabad. Guru Sahib stayed here for seven days. During this time, Guru Sahib resolved the doubts of Raja Hoshang Shah, who became a devotee of Guru Sahib.

data.address: Kushwah Mohalla, Betma, Distt :- Indore, Madhya Pradesh 453001
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Charan Paduka Sahib, Betma,

After descending from Mount Abu, SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI continued spreading the message of Satnam (the True Name) and arrived in Dharanagari. According to ancient stories, Dharanagari was known by the name of King Gopichand. In this region, the Bhil tribe caused great terror and unrest. GURU SAHIB gave them teachings of peace and brotherhood, helping to bring harmony to the area. During his stay, GURU SAHIB also had a baoli (stepwell) dug, which produced very sweet water. This baoli still exists at this holy site today. GURU SAHIB camped here in Kushwah Mohalla.

SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, while walking along the Narmada River, arrived at this place. The Narmada River could only be crossed from this Gwari Ghat. Here, GURU SAHIB met Sharbhang Rishi and resolved his doubts. After crossing the river from here, GURU SAHIB proceeded to the inner part of Jabalpur city.

Gurdwara Shri Raj Ghat Sahib, Burhanpur

SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI visited the city of Burhanpur and set up camp inside the fort on the banks of the Tapti River. Guru Sahib came here during his return from the South and met his devotee, Jeevan Das. After staying here for a few days, Guru Sahib imparted spiritual teachings to the local Sangat (congregation).

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Nanak Tilla Sahib
data.address: Bhuteshwar Rd, Kishor Pura, Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh 281121
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Nanak Tilla Sahib, Vrindavan

This sacred place, located in the city of Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh, has been blessed by the presence of both SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI and SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI

SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI :- GURU SAHIB visited this place during his first Udasi (spiritual journey). Upon arriving in Mathura, Guru Sahib set up camp in a garden on the outskirts of the city.

SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI :- After the death of Aurangzeb, Bahadur Shah ascended the throne with the help of the Sikh forces. In gratitude, Bahadur Shah invited Guru Sahib to Agra. While traveling from Delhi to Agra, Guru Sahib stayed at this place.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Nanak Bagichi Sahib
data.address: Masani Rd, Sarai Azamabad, Distt :- Mathura, Uttar Pradesh 281003
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Nanak Bagichi Sahib , Mathura

This sacred place, located in the city of Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, has been blessed by the presence of SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI. GURU SAHIB stayed in Mathura four months with Bhai Mardana Ji. Initially, Guru Sahib halted at a place near Gau Ghat, but due to rising water levels in the Yamuna River, they moved to this spot. The water at this site was salty, and the Sangat suggested relocating. However, Guru Sahib said, "Kartaar will take care of it." He then instructed Bhai Mardana Ji to draw water from the well, and when Bhai Mardana Ji did so, the water came out sweet. Guru Sahib stayed at this place for over a month.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Guru Tegbahadur Sahib
data.address: Tilak Dwar, Near Kans Tilla, Old Mathura City, Uttar Pradesh
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib, Mathura

This sacred place, located in the city of Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, has been blessed by the presence of SRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI, SRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI, and SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI. Along with them, Mata Ajit Kaur Ji, Mata Sahib Kaur Ji, Mata Sundari Ji, Bhai Gurdas Ji, and the great martyr of the Sikh Panth, Bhai Mani Singh Ji, also spread the teachings of Gurmat at this site.

SRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI :- Guru Sahib halted at this place while traveling to Agra.

SRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI :- Guru Sahib visited this place during his journey to Assam and stayed for 15 days. While here, Guru Sahib preached Sikh teachings and appointed a man named Dharma Naam as a preacher. The Sangat showed great respect for Guru Sahib. After leaving here, Guru Sahib traveled through Agra, Kanpur, and other places, eventually reaching Patna.

SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI :- Guru Sahib stopped at this place both on his way to and returning from Delhi.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Nirmohgarh Sahib
data.address: Village :- Fatehpur Bunga, Teh :- Anandpur Sahib, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Nirmohgarh Sahib, Fatehpur Bunga

This sacred site is located in the village of Fatehpur Bunga in the district of Rupnagar, under the jurisdiction of Tehsil Anandpur Sahib. After the battle of Lohgarh, SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, responding to repeated pleas and false oaths from the hill chieftains, left the fort of Anandpur Sahib and arrived at this location to rest.

One day, during an ongoing congregation, the hill chieftains launched an attack on GURU SAHIB using a cannon. In this assault, GURU SAHIB’s devoted servant, Bhai Ram Singh Ji, was martyred. When the enemy prepared to fire another cannonball, GURU SAHIB quickly shot an arrow from his bow, killing the cannon operator. This forced the hill chieftains to retreat in defeat once again.

The Raja of Basali, who was a devout follower of GURU SAHIB, requested GURU SAHIB to cross the Sutlej River and come to his kingdom. The Raja also negotiated with the other hill chieftains, convincing them not to object if GURU SAHIB entered his territory. The chieftains agreed and promised not to attack. However, as soon as GURU SAHIB and his forces began crossing the Sutlej, the hill chieftains once again betrayed their word and launched another attack.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Dasvin Sahib
data.address: Village :- Ghanaula, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Patshahi Dasvin Sahib, Ghanoula

This sacred site is located in the village of Ghanoula, district Rupnagar. It holds the honor of being blessed twice by SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI's holy presence. The first time GURU SAHIB came to this place was while returning from Nahan. The second visit occurred after GURU SAHIB left the fort of Anandpur Sahib. During this visit, GURU SAHIB was accompanied by Bhai Alam Singh and Bhai Daya Singh. From this very location, GURU SAHIB entrusted a Singh with the responsibility of sending Mata Sundar Kaur Ji and Mata Sahib Kaur Ji to Delhi.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Manji Sahib
data.address: National Highway 21, Bharatgarh, Punjab 140114
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Manji Sahib, Bharatgarh

This sacred site is located in the village of Bharatgarh, district Rupnagar. Bharatgarh is situated on the road between Rupnagar and Sri Anandpur Sahib. When the Kashmiri Pandits approached SRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI for help in saving their religion, GURU SAHIB promised them every possible assistance. On the 11th of Harh, Samvat 1732, after offering prayers at Sri Anandpur Sahib, GURU SAHIB set out on his journey. He stayed at this place on the first night and connected the gathered congregation with Naam (the divine name) and Gurbani. The next day, GURU SAHIB proceeded from here, traveling through Bahadurgarh and Patiala, before eventually reaching Agra, where he voluntarily gave himself up for arrest.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Mithasar Sahib
data.address: Near Kotla Power House, Kiratpur Sahib Anandpur Sahib Road, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Sri Mithasar Sahib , Shergarh

This sacred site is located in the Ropar district near Kotla Power House, on the Ropar-Anandpur Sahib road. SRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI, SRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI , and SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI visited this place and sanctified it with their presence.

SRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI : Nearby this place, there lived a lion. Hearing the plea of the devotees, GURU SAHIB came to this location. He woke up the sleeping lion and hunted it. The devotees requested GURU SAHIB as there was no water source. GURU SAHIB struck the earth with his spear, and sweet water sprang forth. GURU SAHIB often had lunch with the devotees here. He named the place "Mithasar" and "Shergarh." Accompanying GURU SAHIB were Bhai Bidhi Chand Ji, Emperor Jahangir, and Baba Baloo Ji.

SRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI : While on his martyrdom journey to Delhi, GURU SAHIB stayed here. Accompanying GURU SAHIB were Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, Bhai Dayala Ji, Bhai Shabeg Singh Ji, and Bhai Sabhas Singh Ji. From this location, GURU SAHIB instructed the rest of the Sangat to return.

SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI : GURU SAHIB shot an arrow and a water spring emerged. He then had a well constructed here using bricks brought from the Anandgarh Fort.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib
data.address: Village :- Ghanauli, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Sri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib, Ghanoli

When the Kashmiri Pandits approached SHRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI to save their religion, GURU SAHIB promised them all possible help. On 11th Harh, Samvat 1732, after offering prayers at Sri Anandpur Sahib, GURU SAHIB set out on his journey. The first night, GURU SAHIB stayed at the site of Bharatgarh Sahib. The next day, after crossing the Sarsa River, GURU SAHIB reached Ghanoli. Accompanying GURU SAHIB were Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, Bhai Dayala Ji, Bhai Shabeg Singh Ji, and Bhai Sabhas Singh Ji.

SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI: While traveling from Patna to Anandpur, Mata Nanaki Ji, Mata Gujri Ji, the young GOBIND RAI JI, and the entire family stopped here. The entire family traveled from Lakhnaur, passing through Ropar, Ghanoli, Bharatgarh, and eventually reached Kiratpur Sahib.

On June 1, 1924, the seventh batch of the Jaito Morcha of Gangsar set out from Sri Anandpur Sahib, stopped here for rest, and then proceeded further.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Jand Sahib
data.address: Chamkaur Sahib - Behrampur Bet Road, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Sri Jand Sahib, Bir Guru

On the night of 7th Poh, after the battle with the Mughals, SRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, following the command of the five beloved ones (Panj Piare), left the Kachhi Garhi of Sri Chamkaur Sahib. GURU SAHIB reached this location and rested under a Jand tree. Here, GURU SAHIB disciplined informers named Alfu and Gamu. On the 8th of Poh, GURU SAHIB continued his journey towards Jhar Sahib.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Kushatniwaran Sahib
data.address: SH22, Daroli, Teh :- Anandpur Sahib, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab India, 140133
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Kushatniwaran Sahib, Darroli is situated in Village Darroli (Bhatpur) Tehsil Anandpur Sahib, Distt Ropar.

This sacred site is located in the village of Dhadoli Bhatpur, Tehsil Anandpur Sahib, District Ropar. This place has been blessed by the presence of the sixth Guru, SHRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI. After wars and battles, GURU SAHIB chose this region for permanent settlement and to propagate Gurmat (the Guru's teachings).

On 13th Maghar 1673 Bikrami, GURU SAHIB purchased a large tract of land from Raja Tara Chand of Kehloor. On 13th Harh 1674, he established Mohri and instructed Baba Gurditta Ji to settle in Kiratpur Sahib. While spreading the Guru’s teachings in the Doaba region, GURU SAHIB came to this area. The place was dense with forests, filled with wild animals, but a few families lived on a nearby hill and served GURU SAHIB with great devotion. GURU SAHIB regularly engaged the Sangat (congregation) in Naam Kirtan (devotional singing) and spiritual teachings for many days.

Before departing from this place, GURU SAHIB asked the Sangat if they had any wishes as a token of appreciation for their service to the Guru's house. Bhai Bharta Ji, who had been suffering from leprosy, humbly requested that his family's curse of leprosy be removed. GURU SAHIB blessed him, saying that by the grace of Guru Nanak Ji, their affliction was healed, but warned them to refrain from consuming meat and fish, as it could cause the illness to return. After this, Bhai Bharta Ji was cured, and the place came to be known as "Kusht Nivaran" (leprosy cure). Even today, descendants of Bhai Bharta Ji abstain from eating meat or fish to avoid the resurgence of the disease.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Jandsar Sahib
data.address: Village :- Har Raipur, Har Raipur / Bhokhri, Distt :- Bathinda, Punjab 151102
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Jandsar Sahib, Village Har Raipur

This sacred site is located in the village of Har Raipur, District Bathinda, and is blessed by the presence of SHRI GURU HARRAI SAHIB. GURU SAHIB arrived here with an army of 2,200 horsemen and stayed for 22 days. The land where GURU SAHIB set up camp belonged to Khiali Pandit. The places where GURU SAHIB tethered the horses are still marked by the presence of kikar (acacia) and jand (Prosopis) trees.

Khiali Ram had planned to make a broom from the jand tree branches, but when he returned the next day, he found the branches had already split into three parts. Chaudhary Mohan's son, Kala, was the chief of Meharaj. GURU SAHIB bestowed the royal blessings upon his nephews, Phool and Sandli, at this very site. These blessings eventually led to the formation of the princely states of Nabha and Patiala.

Once, Bhai Bhagat Singh's son, Gora, was waving a fan over GURU SAHIB when Bhai Jassa made a derogatory remark about Gora's religious mother. Bhai Gora, in GURU SAHIB's presence, did not respond, but later, his men killed Jassa near a tree by the village pond.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Burj Sahib
data.address: Village :- Rajgarh, Teh :- Rampura Phull, Distt :- Bathinda, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Burj Sahib is located in the village of Burj Rajgarh in District Bathinda.

SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, while residing in the village of Dina, visited this place several times for walks. Here, GURU SAHIB gave spiritual teachings (Gur Updesh) to the congregation. This village is also known as Burj Mana Wala.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Banota Sahib
data.address: Village :- Ablu, Distt :- Bathinda, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Banota Sahib is located in the village of Ablu in District Bathinda.

SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, upon accepting the request of Bhai Daan Singh Ji, arrived at this place. At that time, Baba Santokh Das Ji was meditating here, and GURU SAHIB had spiritual discussions with him. After brushing his teeth with a twig, GURU SAHIB planted it here, which has now grown into a large tree. Bhai Daan Singh Ji told GURU SAHIB that he wanted to establish a village in the name of his grandfather Bhai Ablu Ji, but the descendants of Baba Mehime were not allowing him to do so. GURU SAHIB, from this location, shot an arrow towards the south and told Bhai Daan Singh Ji, "Wherever this arrow lands, you can establish the village there. No one will stop you." Bhai Daan Singh Ji marked the spot where the arrow landed and founded the village.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Teer Sahib
data.address: Village :- Ablu, Distt :- Bathinda, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Teer Sahib is located in the village of Abloo, District Bathinda.

SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI came here at the request of Bhai Daan Singh Ji. Bhai Daan Singh Ji told GURU SAHIB that he wished to establish a village in the name of his great grandfather Bhai Abloo Ji, but the descendants of Baba Mehma were not allowing it. From the site of Gurdwara Shri Banota Sahib, GURU SAHIB shot an arrow towards the south and instructed Bhai Daan Singh Ji to establish the village where the arrow landed, assuring him that no one would stop him. Bhai Daan Singh Ji marked the spot where the arrow landed and founded the village there.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Shatranj Sahib
data.address: Village :- Bassian, Raikot Jagraon Road, Distt :- Ludhiana, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Shatranj Sahib, Basian

This sacred site is located in the village of Basiyan in the Ludhiana district. SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, on his journey from Anandpur Sahib to Damdama Sahib, stayed with Rai Kalla in Raikot. During his stay in Raikot, Guru Sahib learned about the martyrdom of his younger Sahibzadas (sons). While hunting with Rai Kalla, Guru Sahib often visited this place. Guru Sahib used to play chess here with Rai Kalla. At that time, the area was densely forested. When construction of the Gurdwara Sahib began, chess pieces were found buried at the site. Some of these pieces were taken home by the local villagers.

Historical Background – In Accordance with Charan Chalo Marg Gobind

Before SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI, SHRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI also visited this site. A saint named Faqir Baso used to reside here, and he had a discussion with Guru Sahib. After Guru Sahib departed, the saint built a small memorial (Thara) at the site. The samadhi (memorial) of Faqir Baso is still present within the Gurdwara Sahib.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Beri Sahib
data.address:
Village :- Siloani, Teh :- Raikot, 
Distt :- Ludhiana, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Beri Sahib, Siloani

Located in the village of Siloani, Tehsil Raikot, District Ludhiana, this sacred place has been blessed by the presence of SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI. GURU SAHIB visited this site along with Bhai Daya Singh Ji, Bhai Dharam Singh Ji, and Bhai Man Singh Ji. At this location, GURU SAHIB set up camp near a pond. While using a Beri tree twig to clean his teeth, GURU SAHIB planted it in the ground, and today it has grown into a large Beri tree. GURU SAHIB spent the night at this place. Gurdwara Shri Shatranj Sahib, Basian

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Pehli Sahib
data.address: Village :- Kiri Afghana, Distt :- Gurdaspur, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Sri Patshahi Pehli Sahib, Kiri Afgana

This sacred place, located in the village of Kiri Afgana in District Gurdaspur, is blessed by the footsteps of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. GURU SAHIB, traveling from Achal Batala, reached here near the Beas River with Bhai Mardana Ji. At that time, the village had a significant population of Afghans (Pathans). The village chief, upon hearing the words of GURU SAHIB, became a Sikh.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Shaheed ganj Sahib
data.address: Village :- Dale Chak, Distt :- Gurdaspur, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Sri Shaheed Ganj Sahib, Dale Chak

The village of Dale Chak, located in District Gurdaspur, is blessed by the presence of SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI’s holy feet. A Muslim named Abdul Rehman lived in this village. When he found out that an elderly woman named Kirari in the village was a devout follower of SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI and offered butter daily in his name, he, in his arrogance, scolded the woman, claiming that no one could be greater than him.

Hearing the woman's prayer, GURU NANAK SAHIB, along with Bhai Mardana Ji and Bhai Ajite Randhawa, came to this place. GURU SAHIB sent Bhai Mardana Ji to deliver a message to the woman. Abdul Rehman, too, heard of Guru Sahib’s arrival, and in his arrogance and anger, went to confront him. However, upon having a vision of GURU SAHIB, his heart was purified. The butter brought by Mata Ji was enjoyed by GURU SAHIB, Bhai Mardana Ji, and Bhai Ajite Randhawa.

Around 1924-25, some mischief-makers among the local Muslims stole a copy of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji from the village Gurdwara and desecrated it by tearing it apart at this location. The sangat (devotees) recovered the torn scripture, performed its cremation rites, and buried the ashes here. After this incident, the place became known as Shaheed Ganj Sahib.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Flahi Sahib
data.address: Village : Wadala Granthian, Teh :- Batala, Distt :- Gurdaspur, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Flahi Sahib, Wadala Granthian

Located in the village of Wadala Granthian, Tehsil Batala, District Gurdaspur, this place is sanctified by the presence of SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI. GURU SAHIB's marriage took place on 7th Bhadon, in the year 1544, with Mata Sulakhni Ji at Dera Sahib, Batala. The next day, GURU SAHIB visited this place early in the morning. Here, Baba Ji brushed his teeth with a 'flahi' twig and buried it in the ground before bathing. The villagers started revering this place. A celebration is held here the day after GURU SAHIB's wedding.

data.name: Gurdwara Sri Bhavikhat Sahib
data.address: Opp Panj Pyara Park, Anandpur Sahib, Distt :- Ropar, Punjab, India
data.description:
GURUDWARA SHRI BHAVIKHAT SAHIB is located in Anandpur Sahib.

SHRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI, while traveling from Kartarpur to Kiratpur, stopped upon seeing a scenic place. He dismounted from his horse, drank water, and rested for a while. Here, GURU SAHIB looked towards Kesgarh Sahib and offered his salutations. When Bhai Bidhi Chand Ji inquired, GURU SAHIB said, "Bidhi Chand Ji, in my tenth incarnation, I will come here to accomplish many great deeds. Here, the foundation of the Khalsa Panth will be laid, and wars against oppression will be fought." At this place, there are two Gurudwara Sahibs with a same history. Gurudwara Shri Bohar Sahib managed by the Missal Shaheedan Tarnadal, while Gurudwara Shri Bhavikhat Sahib is under the care of Baba Bidhi Chand Dal. This site also has an old banyan tree and an ancient well.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib
data.address: Village :- Bhagrana, Distt :- Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib, Bhagrana

This Gurdwara Sahib is located in the village of Bhagrana in the Fatehgarh Sahib district. SHRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI visited here during his journey through the Malwa region to spread Gurmat (Sikh teachings). Bhai Diala Ji, a resident of this village, along with the local Sangat (congregation), served GURU SAHIB greatly. Pleased with their service, GURU SAHIB had a well constructed here. GURU SAHIB visited here a second time during his journey of martyrdom. Bhai Diala Ji continued to serve GURU SAHIB with devotion. GURU SAHIB instructed Bhai Diala Ji to send his two sons, Baba Madan Ji and Baba Kotha Ji, to Guru Gobind Rai Ji. After reaching Anandpur Sahib, both brothers served Guru Gobind Rai Ji with great devotion and were blessed with Amrit (initiation) to become Singhs.

Baba Madan Ji and Baba Kotha Ji attained martyrdom alongside Sahibzada Ajit Singh Ji and Sahibzada Jujhar Singh Ji in the Battle of Chamkaur, fighting with forty Singhs.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Thara Sahib Patshahi Chevin
data.address: Old Tehsil Road, BBSBE College Campus, Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab 140407
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Thara Sahib Patshahi Chevin, Fatehgarh Sahib

This holy site is located in Fatehgarh Sahib city, in front of the Secretariat. SHRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI, the master of both spiritual and temporal authority (Miri Piri), came to this place while spreading the teachings of the faith. In memory of GURU SAHIB's visit, a platform (Thara Sahib) was constructed here, where Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji is now enshrined. Next to this Gurdwara Sahib, there is also an old bridge. Bhai Dhanna Singh Ji writes that this bridge over the stream was built by SHRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI. GURU SAHIB came here from the village of Ranwan and then proceeded to the village of Brahman Majra. The area where the village of Brahman Majra was located is now within the city of Sirhind.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Nauvi and Dasvi Sahib
data.address: Village :- Ugani, Teh :- Rajpura, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Patshahi Nauvi and Dasvi Sahib, Ugani

This place is located in the village of Ugani, Tehsil Rajpura, District Patiala. SHRI GURU TEGBAHADUR SAHIB JI passed through here on his martyrdom journey while traveling to Delhi. Guru Sahib stayed here for two nights. SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI also visited this place and sanctified it by touching his feet. Initially, separate places were dedicated to both Guru Sahibs, but later, one common place was created.

data.name: Gurudwara Shaheed Baba Jai Singh Khalakat Sahib
data.address: Village :- Baran, Patiala Sirhind Road, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurudwara Shaheed Baba Jai Singh Khalakat Ji belonged to the village of Barn in District Patiala.

He lived there with his family, which included his wife, Mata Dhan Kaur, his two sons, Bhai Kadaka Singh Ji and Bhai Khadak Singh Ji, and his two daughters-in-law. In the year 1810 (Samvat calendar), Nawab Abdus Samad Khan of Sirhind was traveling with his army from Sirhind to Patiala. When he reached near the village Mughal Majra (now known as Barn), he instructed his soldiers to find a Singh (Sikh) to carry some of his belongings. At that time, Baba Jai Singh Ji was bathing at the village well and was unaware of the Nawab’s arrival. The Nawab grew furious that Baba Jai Singh Ji had not come to greet him. The soldiers captured Baba Ji and brought him before the Nawab. The Nawab was pleased to see him, thinking that he could now punish Baba Ji. He questioned, "Why did you not greet us when we passed by your village ?" Baba Ji humbly replied, "I was unaware of your arrival, as my mind was absorbed in the remembrance of GURU SAHIB."The Nawab, filled with rage, said, "We will decide your fate in Patiala. For now, you will carry this load to Patiala." Baba Ji asked what the load contained ?, and the soldiers replied that it was the Nawab’s hookah. Baba Ji firmly responded, "I will not carry a load that includes a hookah." Angered by this, the Nawab summoned Baba Ji's family and commanded them to carry the load. They, too, refused, stating, "We are Amritdhari (baptized Sikhs) and cannot carry a hookah." In his rage, the Nawab ordered the execution of Baba Ji’s family, one by one, in front of him. Only Baba Ji's younger daughter-in-law, who was pregnant and had gone to her parental home in Ambala, survived. Finally, the Nawab martyred Baba Ji by hanging him upside down from a tree, flaying his back, and killing him. Later, the villagers came together and cremated the five martyrs at the site of their martyrdom.Baba Ji’s younger daughter-in-law later gave birth to a son in Ambala, ensuring the continuation of their lineage.

data.name: Gurudwara Bhai Tara Singh Ji Shaheed
data.address: Village :- Waan, Distt :- Taran Taaran, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Bhai Tara Singh Sahib is situated in the village of Wan in the Tarn Taran district.

Bhai Tara Singh Wan was born in this village. He was a devout and disciplined Sikh, always ready and prepared. Historical accounts mention that he wore a blue attire. He was often seen engrossed in reading Gurbani. Bhai Tara Singh established a camp on his farmland outside the village, where he arranged lodging and langar (community kitchen) for visiting devotees. Along with being a person of spiritual devotion and remembrance of Gurbani, Bhai Tara Singh was also a courageous warrior. He fought several battles during the era of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur. During the Mughal rule, Punjab followed a feudal land management system. The village chiefs often oppressed the common people. The chief of the village of Naushera, Sahib Rai, was arrogant and tyrannical. He would allow his horses to graze in the fields of Sikhs. One day, the Sikhs collectively requested the chief to keep his horses away from their fields. The chief arrogantly replied that they should braid ropes from their hair for his horses. This insulting remark deeply hurt the Sikhs, who reported the matter to S. Amar Singh and S. Baghel Singh in the nearby village of Bhusse.

S. Amar Singh and S. Baghel Singh seized the chief's horses and sold them in Patiala to Ala Singh. They used the proceeds to contribute to the langar at Bhai Tara Singh Wan's dera. When the chief learned about this, he discovered that the horses were taken by Amar Singh and Baghel Singh, and Baghel Singh was staying at Bhai Tara Singh's dera. The chief, accompanied by a few men, went to the dera in anger and started speaking harshly. Despite Bhai Tara Singh's attempts to pacify him, the chief did not relent. The Singhs then gave him a fitting response. Furious, the chief complained to the Faujdar (local military commander) of Patti. The Faujdar of Patti, Zafar Beg, gathered a force of 200 horsemen and launched an attack on Bhai Tara Singh’s dera. At the time, S. Baghel Singh had gone to fetch water early in the morning. He encountered the advancing troops and engaged in combat. Hearing the sounds of gunfire, the Singhs from the dera joined to support S. Baghel Singh. A fierce battle ensued. During this clash, S. Baghel Singh attained martyrdom, while on the other side, Zafar Beg's two nephews and several others were killed. Zafar Beg himself fled to save his life. Zafar Beg complained to the Subedar of Lahore, Zakaria Khan. Zakaria Khan ordered Momon Khan to attack Bhai Tara Singh and either capture him alive or bring his severed head. Momon Khan, with an army of 2,000 soldiers, marched towards Bhai Tara Singh's dera. A Sikh from Lahore came to inform Bhai Tara Singh of this impending attack.

Bhai Tara Singh prepared fully for the battle. The fight lasted an entire day. One by one, 21 Singhs attained martyrdom, and eventually, Bhai Tara Singh was also martyred. The heads of all the martyred Singhs were placed on spears and taken to Lahore.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Rajo Pujo Falo Fulo Sahib
data.address: Village :- Pilkhani, Teh :- Rajpura, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Rajo Poojo Phalo Phoolo Sahib, Pilkhani test testign

This sacred place is situated in the village of Pilkani, in the Rajpura Tehsil of District Patiala. SHRI GURU TEGH BAHADUR SAHIB JI visited this site. At that time, due to a natural calamity, this village was buried under debris. Since it was settled on ruins, it was earlier known as "Pilkani Thehri." People were hesitant to live in this area, so only a few residents stayed here. When GURU SAHIB visited the nearby village of Ugani, a resident of that village, Bhai Dharma Ji, went to have GURU SAHIB’s darshan. He humbly requested GURU SAHIB to visit his village. Accepting his request, GURU SAHIB came to this place, and the devotees gathered to welcome and honor him with great respect. GURU SAHIB imparted the teachings of remembering and chanting God’s name.

Pleased with the devotion and service of the people, GURU SAHIB gave his blessings and said, "Rajo Poojo, Phalo Phoolo" (meaning "Worship, Flourish, and Prosper"). He also declared that the community kitchen (Langar) will always remain in service at this place, and this land will be filled with prosperity and joy.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Baag Shaheedan Sahib
data.address: Sec 44 A, Chandigarh, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Bagh Shaheedan Sahib, Chandigarh

This sacred site is located in Sector 44 of the modern city of Chandigarh. It is the martyrdom site of Baba Sukha Singh Ji and his fellow warriors. Baba Sukha Singh Ji was the younger brother of Baba Baaz Singh Ji, who was appointed as the Governor of Sirhind by Baba Banda Singh Bahadur. Near this place, in the village of Barael, lived Mughal rulers named Jaula Khan, Rustam Khan, and Shamsh Khan. These rulers had created immense tyranny in the region. Along with looting Hindu property, they also dishonored women. Whenever a wedding procession passed through Barael, these rulers would forcibly seize the bride’s palanquin, take it to their fort in Barael, and disgrace Hindu women for several days before letting them go. The lives of the common people had become unbearable.

Despite multiple pleas and requests from the villagers, the Mughal rulers refused to change their ways. Helpless, the people approached Baba Sukha Singh Ji and narrated their suffering. Moved by their distress, Baba Ji accepted their request and tried to reason with Jaula Khan and his men, explaining that all women should be treated as sisters and daughters. However, intoxicated with power, these rulers ignored his words. Baba Sukha Singh Ji then devised a strategy to expel them from the fort and decided to confront them according to Khalsa traditions. The Khalsa sent a message to the Mughal rulers, deceiving them into believing that a wedding procession of Rajput women carrying immense wealth was arriving from Ropar. Greedy for riches, Jaula Khan and his allies hid in this garden, waiting to ambush the procession. However, when the Mughals attacked, they were shocked and humiliated to find that the palanquins were loaded with stones instead of brides. Meanwhile, the Singhs had already taken control of the Mughal fort. A fierce battle ensued. Baba Sukha Singh Ji first sent a contingent led by Baba Harkirat Singh Ji, who fought valiantly and attained martyrdom while eliminating many Mughals.

Then, Baba Sukha Singh Ji himself entered the battlefield with his warriors, annihilating the tyrants before achieving martyrdom. The enemy was completely destroyed, and the Khalsa emerged victorious.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Kalyansar Sahib
data.address: Village :- Fatehgarh Korotana, Distt :- Moga, India
data.description: GURUDWARA SHRI KALYANSAR SAHIB is situated in the Village Fatehgarh Korotana, Distt. Moga. Situated on Moga Jalandhar road this place marks where SRI GURU HARGOBIND SAHIB JI made stop over while travelling from and to Bhai Ki Daroli several times. A Ber Tree (Jujube Tree) is also present at the back side of Gurdwara Sahib

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Navin Sahib
data.address: Village :- Baurna Kalan, Teh :- Nabha, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib, Ramgarh Borha Kalan

This sacred place in the village of Ramgarh Borha Kalan, Tehsil Nabha, District Patiala, is blessed with the holy presence of SHRI GURU TEGBAHADUR SAHIB JI. GURU SAHIB visited here during his Malwa journey. Accompanying him were Mata Gujri Ji, Mama Kripal Chand Ji, Bhai Sangatia Ji, Bhai Sahib Chand Ji, Bhai Kripal Das Ji, Bhai Diala Ji, Bhai Gurditta Ji, Bhai Uday Ji, Bhai Jaita Ji, and Bhai Nathu Ram Ji. They traveled from Shri Anandpur Sahib via Ghanoli, Ropar, Nandpur Kalor, Tahilpura, No Lakha, Lang Simbro, Dhengera, Agol, and Rohta before reaching this place. GURU SAHIB stayed here for one day and one night.

In the morning and evening, GURU SAHIB blessed the congregation by reciting and singing Gurbani Kirtan. This Gurdwara Sahib also has a beautiful Baoli Sahib (a sacred stepwell), which was established in 1926 by Maharani Shiv Kaur, the wife of Maharaja Bharpur Singh of Nabha state, as an offering of gratitude after her prayers for a child were fulfilled.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Pehli Theh Sahib
data.address: Village :- Issarhail, Chandigarh Sirhind Road, Distt :- Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab, India
data.description:
GURDWARA SRI PATSHAHI PEHLI THEH SAHIB is situated in the Village Issarhel Distt City Fatehgarh Sahib. Its situated on the Chandigarh Sirhind Road.

The First Guru, SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, had graced this mound with his presence. Guru Sahib stayed here for seven days. On this mound, there still exists a Karir (Capparis decidua) shrub. Out of ignorance, people have tried multiple times to uproot it, but it always grows back green and fresh again.

data.name: Gurdwara Shri Manji Sahib
data.address: Village :- Lohsimbli, Teh :- Rajpura, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Manji Sahib, Lohsimbli

This sacred site is located in the village of Lohsimbli, District Patiala. SHRI GURU GOBIND SINGH JI sanctified this place with his holy presence. Before him, SHRI GURU TEGBAHADUR SAHIB JI also came here while traveling from Nanheri. GURU SAHIB set up a langar (community kitchen) here by heating iron, and the name of the village was changed from Nosimbli to Lohsimbli. At one time, a merchant was passing by with his mules loaded with goods. A fierce storm and strong winds began to blow. The merchant prayed before Guru Gobind Singh Ji, seeking protection. Hearing his plea, GURU SAHIB protected him. Out of gratitude, the merchant offered a cot (charpai) as a donation. GURU SAHIB instructed his Singhs to take this cot further along. However, the local caretakers (priests) said it would be of no use ahead. GURU SAHIB replied, “If it is of no use ahead, then it will not be of any use here either.” GURU SAHIB’s words proved true—the cot has never been fully used to this day. Its length keeps increasing and decreasing mysteriously. This cot is still present and displayed at the site.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Navin Sahib
data.address: Village :- Simbro, Distt :- Patiala, Punjab, India
data.description:
Gurudwara Shri Patshahi Nauvin Sahib, Simbro

When Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji set out from Anandpur Sahib on a journey to Assam, he blessed the land of Malwa. Guru Sahib passed through villages like Nandpur Kalor, Dadu Majra, Ugani, Harpalpur, Kuba, Kheri, Nolakha, Tehalpura, Akar Lang, and others. During this journey, Mata Nanaki Ji, Mata Gujri Ji, and Mama Kirpal Das Ji accompanied Guru Sahib. While guiding and uplifting the congregations, Guru Sahib reached Simbro and rested under a banyan tree. Guru Sahib stayed here for three days and imparted the teachings of Naam (the Divine Name) and Gurbani to the devotees.

data.name: Gurudwara Shri Guru Tegbahadur Sahib Ji
data.address: Raj Mohalla, Jamalpura, City Sonipat, Haryana, India
data.description:
Gurdwara Shri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib is located in the Raj Mohalla area of the city of Sonipat in Haryana.

SHRI GURU TEGBAHADUR SAHIB JI, along with his family, arrived at this place while traveling via Panipat and stayed at the home of Bhai Mishra Ji. Bhai Mishra Ji served the Guru with great devotion. After staying here for a few days, the Guru continued his journey towards Assam via Delhi. Before departing, he instructed that a Dharamsala (religious rest house) be built at this place in the name of SHRI GURU NANAK DEV JI. Since then, devotional singing and worship have continued at the site. Another structure was built in front of this location, during the construction of which ancient weapons were found — including two swords and a shield — which are now respectfully displayed in the Gurdwara Sahib.
